notes.text: WORKFLOW: non-24 sleep-wake (blind participant). The human counterpart to the free-running mouse. With no light input reaching the clock, the rhythm runs at its OWN period (tau = 24.5 h here) rather than the day's, so it drifts about half an hour later every day and the sleep window walks all the way around the clock over roughly seven weeks. Read the double-plotted actogram first: a rhythm at exactly 24 h would sit vertical, and this one leans. Then read the periodogram peak, which recovers tau numerically. Free-running is not a rodent-only phenomenon; this is a recognised clinical presentation, and the drift is why sleep complaints in these patients come and go on a cycle.
